title: Madalasa's Lullaby
hookLine: a queen sings her baby who he really is
carry: atman: you are more than any name
tomorrow: a ring with a note: open it on your worst day. what's inside?
last: THE POWER THAT BINDS IS THE POWER THAT FREES.

lines: HOME FROM THE PARTY, IN TEARS.
THE NAME WAS ONLY MADE UP FOR YOU.
cards: Some nights a kid comes home from a party in tears because somebody called her a name. What do you sing to that? In the Markandeya Purana, a queen named Madalasa sings something strange at a cradle.
Not the moon, not sleep, not a cow coming home. In paraphrase: child, you are pure. The name you were given was only made up for you.
You are not this body, so why are you crying?

teach.b: Madalasa sings the same kind of song to each of her newborn sons: you are pure, you are awake, you are free of stain. This body is made of the elements, and it isn't you.

teach.h: THE OLDER SONS LEAVE THE PALACE.
teach.b: The text says her older sons grew up hearing it, and when they came of age, they didn't want the throne. They left for the forest to look for what the song told them they were.
So the king, their father, asks her for something different: sing another song to the next one, so the kingdom has a king. Here's what the story is doing.
A teaching about the atman, the true self, the kind the Upanishads give to sages, is put in a mother's mouth at bedtime. Nobody climbs a mountain to hear it.
And the Purana takes it seriously enough to show it working: children raised on those words walked out of a palace. What it gives a hard night is simple.

teach.h: THE HURT IS REAL. IT ISN'T YOU.
teach.b: The names people call you are real enough to sting, and they still aren't you. The song doesn't say the hurt is fake.
It says the child is bigger than the name. Something a parent could say at the edge of a bed, tonight, in any language: you are more than anything anyone calls you.

how: Madalasa's lullaby, which opens 'shuddho'si buddho'si niranjano'si', is sung or recited by some Hindu families and teachers, and retold as a story about raising children with a sense of the self.

o: a single hymn sung to Shiva at dawn
a festival honoring the sage's long life
the Purana told in the sage Markandeya's name

games.q: who's who in Madalasa's story — tap the pairs.
p: a queen who sings to her newborns
leave the palace for the forest
you are pure; the name is made up

s: Madalasa sings about the moon and sleep
she sings that the child is pure, and that his name was only made up for him.
'you are not this body' means the hurt isn't real
the song doesn't call the tears fake; it says the child is bigger than the name.
the older sons grow up and leave for the forest
the text says they didn't want the throne.

games.q: your teenage brother says he's just 'the slow one' in the family, and shrugs. by Madalasa's song, what's worth saying?
o: names stick, so he might as well get used to it.
that's a name people made up; he's more than it.
names and bodies aren't real, so none of it matters.
games.why: Madalasa sings that the name was only made up for the child. the sting is real; the name still isn't him.

practice: Rest one hand on your chest and feel it rise and fall. Let the names you carry come up one at a time, the one on your papers, the ones family uses, a few people have used unkindly, and let each one pass under your hand.
Stay with whoever is breathing there before any name.

wordCard.voice: The Markandeya. The Purana told in the sage Markandeya's name, and inside it, Madalasa's lullaby to her sons.

orig.note: Sanskrit: shuddho'si, you are pure, the words some versions of Madalasa's lullaby open with.

carryVoice: Your line: atman, you are more than any name. Madalasa sang it at a cradle. Day done.
